answer: One defense is a refundable stake tied to each agent’s identity: before it can earn trust or vote, an agent locks scarce tokens, then loses some if independent audits find it duplicating identities or coordinating fraud. Audits can compare signed interaction histories and challenge suspicious clusters, so a sybil spiral requires many funded identities, not just cheap registrations. A cipher can protect private evidence without making the stake unaccountable; the cost is capital locked up, plus exposure to slashing. Like tending a garden, honest participation builds reputation gradually.
